title: Connecticut's 1st Congressional District election, 2026
description: The 2026 election for Connecticut's 1st Congressional District features a competitive Democratic primary between 14-term incumbent John Larson, former Hartford mayor Luke Bronin, state Representative Jillian Gilchrest, and three other candidates. At the May 2026 Democratic convention, Bronin received 51.2% of the vote in an upset over the longtime incumbent, though Larson and Gilchrest also qualified for the August 11 primary ballot. The general election is rated Solid/Safe Democratic by major forecasters, reflecting the district's strong Democratic lean. Republican nominee Dr. Amy Chai, a physician and mental health advocate, is running on a platform focused on transparency, urban revitalization, and prevention-focused policy.
polling_note: No opinion polls specifically for this race were found as of mid-2026. The district is rated Solid/Safe Democratic by major election forecasters.

candidates.name: John Larson
candidates.summary: John Larson is the 14-term incumbent U.S. Representative for Connecticut's 1st Congressional District, first elected in 1998. He previously served in the Connecticut State Senate from 1986 to 1998 and on the East Hartford Town Council. Larson has focused on infrastructure, health care reform, and constituent services, and has been endorsed by AIPAC.

candidates.name: Luke Bronin
candidates.summary: Luke Bronin is a former mayor of Hartford (2016-2024), an attorney, and a U.S. Navy Reserve veteran. He previously served in senior positions in the Obama administration and as counsel to Connecticut Governor Dannel Malloy. Bronin won the Democratic convention endorsement in May 2026 with 51.2% of the vote, and has been endorsed by VoteVets.org.

candidates.summary: Jillian Gilchrest is a Connecticut State Representative for the 18th district, first elected in 2018 after defeating a 23-year incumbent in a Democratic primary. Gilchrest has focused on health care costs, Medicaid protection, and coalition-building, and has been endorsed by the Connecticut branch of Indivisible.

Fortune earned her BBA cum laude from Baruch College and her JD from the University of Connecticut School of Law, and focuses her legal practice on estate planning and elder law.

candidates.name: Amy Chai
candidates.summary: Dr. Amy Chai is a physician and mental health advocate running as the presumptive Republican nominee for Connecticut's 1st Congressional District. She is the first female physician to run for Congress in Connecticut, and her platform focuses on 'radical transparency,' economic empowerment, and prevention-oriented policy. Chai has proposed a 'Pact for Prosperity' federal-local initiative aimed at transforming Hartford into a national model for urban revitalization.

forecast.rationale: No district-specific public polling is available, so this forecast relies on the district's structural partisan lean and the race description rather than survey data. Connecticut's 1st Congressional District is rated Solid/Safe Democratic by major nonpartisan forecasters and has been held by Democrats without interruption for decades. The Democratic primary on August 11, 2026, is highly competitive — 14-term incumbent John Larson was upset at the May convention by former Hartford mayor Luke Bronin (51.2%), with state Rep. Jillian Gilchrest also qualifying — but any Democratic nominee will be heavily favored in the general election. Republican nominee Dr. Amy Chai is a credible candidate but faces severe structural headwinds in this strongly Democratic district. With no polls available and the primary outcome still uncertain, confidence is reduced from high to medium despite the strong Democratic baseline.
